_about: One entry per match, in the order the site shows them (DFL matches first: they have the better tracking). Every per-match fact the pipeline needs lives here. raw_dir is relative to the data folder's parent (the project root by default; see pipeline/paths.py). chapter_urls files live in the output folder. See docs/ADDING-A-MATCH.md.

source.dataset: DFL/IDSSE open data (Bassek et al. 2025, Scientific Data), CC-BY 4.0, (c) DFL
source.convert: python3 providers/dfl_to_pff.py <dfl folder> DFL-MAT-J03WMX 182265 data/182265 --home-name "Köln" --away-name "Bayern Munich" --home-code KOE --away-code FCB

matches.title: Köln vs Bayern Munich
matches.label: Köln vs Bayern Munich (Bundesliga)
matches.hub_note: The first match from outside the PFF World Cup set: DFL open data from the Bundesliga (CC-BY 4.0, © DFL), converted to the pipeline's format. The tracking is real 25 Hz optical data, resampled to the pipeline's 29.97 fps. The events are the DFL feed, snapped to the tracked ball. DFL has no analyst "under pressure" tag, so the engaged/passive threshold is pooled from the World Cup matches instead of calibrated on this one. The final day of the season: Bayern won 2-1 with an 89th-minute goal.

matches.title: Morocco vs Spain
matches.sub: World Cup round of 16 · 0-0 after extra time, Morocco won 3-0 on penalties
matches.competition: FIFA World Cup 2022 · Round of 16 · Education City Stadium
matches.label: Morocco vs Spain (Round of 16)
matches.hub_note: Classifies each team's out-of-possession phase (High Press / Mid Block / Low Block / Transition) from back-line depth and inter-line compactness only.

matches.title: France vs Morocco
matches.competition: FIFA World Cup 2022 · Semifinal · Al Bayt Stadium
matches.label: Morocco vs France (Semifinal)
matches.hub_note: Same classification logic as the Morocco vs Spain baseline: back-line depth + inter-line compactness only. This match's raw tracking data has no per-player speed field (unlike 10508), so the pressure-on-ball-carrier score falls back to a fixed max-speed assumption per player instead of an empirically-derived one -- see the methodology doc.

matches.title: Germany vs Japan
matches.sub: World Cup group stage · Japan won 2-1
matches.competition: FIFA World Cup 2022 · Group Stage · Khalifa International Stadium
matches.label: Japan vs Germany (Group Stage)
matches.hub_note: Same classification logic as the other two matches: back-line depth + inter-line compactness only. Like 10515, this match's raw tracking has no per-player speed field, so the pressure-on-ball-carrier score uses each player's own empirically derived max speed (from smoothed-position deltas) rather than a flat assumption -- see the methodology doc. Japan came back from 0-1 down to win 2-1.

matches.title: Belgium vs Canada
matches.sub: World Cup group stage · Belgium won 1-0
matches.competition: FIFA World Cup 2022 · Group Stage · Ahmad Bin Ali Stadium
matches.label: Belgium vs Canada (Group Stage)
matches.hub_note: Same classification logic as the other matches: back-line depth + inter-line compactness only. Like Germany vs Japan, this match's raw tracking has no per-player speed field, so the pressure-on-ball-carrier score uses each player's own empirically derived max speed rather than a flat assumption -- see the methodology doc. Belgium sat deep to protect an early goal; Canada dominated territorially and missed a penalty, and lost 1-0.

matches.title: Argentina vs France
matches.sub: World Cup final · 3-3 after extra time, Argentina won 4-2 on penalties
matches.competition: FIFA World Cup 2022 · Final · Lusail Stadium
matches.label: Argentina vs France (Final)

keeper_swap.why: tracking labels the two keepers the wrong way round in extra time (checked against shots and Mbappe's 118' penalty)

matches.hub_note: Same classification logic as the other matches: back-line depth + inter-line compactness only. Unlike matches 2-4, this match's raw tracking DOES carry a per-player speed field (like the Morocco vs Spain baseline), so the pressure-on-ball-carrier score uses each player's own real tracked max speed -- see the methodology doc. One of the wildest finals in World Cup history: Argentina led 2-0, France drew level 2-2 in a two-minute Mbappe burst late in regulation, Argentina led again in extra time, Mbappe completed his hat-trick to make it 3-3, and Argentina won 4-2 on penalties.
